column3: Direct parallel: Hell is the collective appointed meeting-point, sharpening its prepared, intercepting role.
The separating Day is fixed for all, supplying the timed collective setting for the ambush.
Direct lexical parallel: the Lord is at the watchpost, keeping surveillance and requital together without collapsing them.
Places the guilty in enduring Hell-punishment; strong destination context, though not the watchpost image itself.
Immediate continuation: it specifies prolonged staying within the place named as a watchpost.
The guarded listening-post and its projectile show r-s-d as active protection/interception; a distinct celestial scene.
A condemned speaker's wish for final cessation contrasts with the continuing, prepared consequence of 78:21.
Immediate scene: opened skies establish movement and access just before the ambushing destination.
Angelic guards set before and behind a messenger supply a secondary r-s-d surveillance image, not Hell's function.
Return to wrongdoing brings renewed consequence, with Hell framed as a confining enclosure for disbelievers.
Warning establishes the addressed living hearer and the word becoming due against disbelievers; indirect accountability context.
Direct Hell reference: its punishment is binding, reinforcing 78:21 as an inescapable prepared consequence.
Immediate continuation: identifies the transgressors as those for whom the destination functions as return.
The single cry and extinguishing are a distant judgment scene, without the prepared-watchpost relation.
Immediate context: the trumpet gathers people in groups, providing the arriving movement that the watchpost meets.
The hostile human irsad establishes an active waiting/ambush usage; secondary and contrary to the divine judgment scene.
Divine command realizing what is willed supports inevitability generally, not the destination or surveillance image.
A single cry brings all before the divine presence, supplying collective presentation before judgment.
Immediate later explanation: refusal to expect reckoning helps identify the accountability setting of the watchpost.
Contrary destination: faithful works receive gardens, clarifying the judgmental polarity but not the ambush image.
Their lack of reprieve after destruction only remotely supports fixed consequence.
Names Hell-fire as consequence for persecutors who do not repent; it adds conditional moral context.
Immediate continuation: specifies the exceptional provisions encountered within the place.
The challenge to desire death is a remote afterlife test, not a description of Hell as watchpost.
A demand to restore ancestors is only a polemical resurrection context.
The command to sit at every ambush gives a human tactical parallel for active interception; it is not a model for 78:21.
Immediate context: the Day of Separation is fixed in time, anchoring the scene in an appointed judgment.
Direct declaration of the promised Hell strongly confirms destination and prior warning, without adding r-s-d nuance.
Immediate realization by command supports certainty abstractly, with no watchpost or Hell relation.
Prepared restraints and blazing fire provide close punitive equipment/context for a prearranged Hell.
Immediate upheaval context: vanishing mountains complete the approach to the watchpost scene.
An enclosing fire supplies confinement imagery, secondary to the active interception in 78:21.
Forgetting God and self-forgetfulness provide distant moral background, not the stated destination.
The command to cast the stubborn denier into Hell makes entry and individualized judgment explicit.
Immediate continuation: negates cooling and drink in the place, detailing its punitive character.
The Lord's seeing supplies a surveillance/accountability resonance, though not the lexical watchpost image.
Entry through Hell's gates and abiding there make the prepared destination concrete for the arrogant.
Hell encircling disbelievers provides a strong enclosure parallel, distinct from the watchpost's interception.
A prior word and named term defer an otherwise binding consequence; secondary timing context.
A fire closed over them reinforces enclosure, but does not specify the path or those intercepted.
Book revelation from the Mighty, Wise does not materially clarify 78:21.
Being turned aside by prior worship offers distant obstruction imagery and a disbelieving context.
The promised event's apparent brevity when seen supports inevitability and imminence, not the watchpost image.
Calls Hell an evil settlement and stay, directly complementing 78:21's destination language.
Creaturely fear and obedience provide broad judgment background only.
Directly identifies the blazing fire as refuge/destination; close but less specific than 78:21.
Sudden emergence after the blast supplies only the wider resurrection sequence.
Affirms the dispute of fire's people as reality, adding internal consequence context.
Granted respite is only a remote temporal parallel to appointed consequence.
Arrogant refusal of worship culminates in humbled entry into Hell, linking conduct and destination.
The split sky parallels the eschatological sky transformation, secondary to 78:19-21.
The remaining wife in Lot's story is a distant instance of exclusion from rescue.
Turning away from signs is general antecedent conduct, without a particular Hell/watchpost contribution.
Hell explicitly prepared as reception for disbelievers strongly supports its prior preparation, while retaining a contrasting hospitality term.
Earlier deniers' outcome offers generic precedent for consequence.
The accusation concerning Mary's family does not clarify the judgment scene.
Granted respite is a remote term-related parallel only.
Lot's rescue and his wife's exclusion give a distant allocation pattern, not Hell's watchpost role.
The known appointed time offers timing language but little on 78:21 itself.
Lot's rescue from a corrupt town supplies broad judgment contrast only.
Denial of resurrection is background for the Day, but adds no destination detail.
Knowledge of who is in the town and selective rescue weakly parallels differentiated judgment.
The trumpet day, divine sovereignty, and knowledge of hidden and visible provide broad eschatological surveillance context.
Directly assigns disbelievers to abiding Hell-fire, strongly confirming the class and enduring destination.
Fear of a tremendous Day's punishment supplies individual accountability, without the watchpost image.
Destruction of unjust towns is a distant historical judgment analogue.
Preferring worldly goods over remembrance does not materially clarify Hell as watchpost.
Veiled sight and inability to hear describe receptivity failure, only indirect antecedent context.
Exclusive devotion and submission do not add a specific link to 78:21.
Divine seeing is too general here to clarify the prepared destination.
Opposition spending ends in regret, defeat, and being gathered to Hell; it adds a consequential route.
Angelic questioning and Hell as destination make individualized accounting and a bad return explicit.
An incomplete report of what they used to say adds no usable relation.
The contrast between worldly heat and Hell's fiercer fire strengthens punitive intensity, not watchpost function.
A bad accounting and Hell as abode link response/refusal to judgmental destination.
Gathering hypocrites and disbelievers together in Hell reinforces collective allocation, though in a different setting.
A town's punishment after ingratitude is a historical consequence parallel only.
The Sabbath test and transgression offer a distant accountability pattern.
Repentant belief averts a temporal punishment, providing a contrary route rather than defining the final watchpost.
The appointed character of prayer offers only a formal timing resonance.
Questioning over deeds supports the individual accounting dimension of 78:21.
Witnessing and testing in the community are distant accountability motifs.
Inner disease and painful punishment provide generic moral-consequence context.
Inheritance apportionment does not clarify the eschatological watchpost.
Prophetic instruction and release from burdens do not add a material connection.
Explicitly denies injustice and locates fault in themselves, qualifying Hell's consequence as deserved.
Repeated rebellion and humiliation give only diffuse antecedent wrongdoing context.
Adam's garden prohibition is not a useful parallel to Hell as watchpost.
The assertion that they wronged themselves offers a general self-incurred consequence principle.
Trading guidance for error is a distant route-to-loss image, not the destination scene.
Directly assigns their reckoning to God, strongly reinforcing the accounting dimension alongside the watchpost.
A command from the divine presence does not materially specify 78:21.
A prophet's complaint of denial supplies generic antecedent rejection only.
Mocking the promised event contrasts with its fixed arrival; it is secondary warning context.
The announced destruction of a wrongdoing town is a distant judgment precedent.
Pilgrimage restrictions and expiation do not clarify the eschatological destination.
Talut's appointment and disputed kingship have no material relation here.
Leading criminals' plotting rebounds on themselves, a distant self-incurred consequence parallel.
People's refusal until precedent or face-to-face punishment arrives supplies a contrary warning/arrival frame.
The call to common monotheism does not add a material relation to 78:21.
The path to Hell makes the destination a directed route, closely complementing the watchpost positioned for arrivals.
Sitting at every path to threaten and turn people aside supplies a human, contrary path-interception parallel.
Those made wretched are explicitly in the Fire, adding the enduring condition of its inhabitants.
Hell is appointed for one who chooses the immediate world and turns away, adding a route defined by response.
False objects and their worshippers are named as fuel for Hell, intensifying its active consuming character.
Fire garments and poured scalding liquid give concrete punitive detail for the prepared destination.
Denial of the Hour is paired with a blazing fire prepared for its deniers; it reinforces preparation and warning.
Hell surrounds the disbelievers, a close enclosure parallel to the watchpost's inescapable interception.
The Fire is the evildoers' refuge; repeated attempted exit and return make its holding function explicit.
Disbelievers are driven to Hell in groups and its gates opened, strongly matching movement into a prepared destination.
Shackles and chains precede being dragged, adding coercive capture imagery to Hell's punishment.
Dragging through boiling water and then into the Fire continues the forced-entry sequence.
Enemies of God are gathered toward the Fire and held in ordered ranks, closely supporting collective arrival for judgment.
The people of Hell call for termination and are answered with continued remaining, reinforcing persistence within it.
Being forgotten in the Fire after treating the meeting-day as mockery adds reciprocal accountability and permanence.
A blazing Fire is prepared for disbelievers, directly supporting the prearranged character of 78:21.
The condemned are driven violently toward Hell-fire, making arrival at the destination active rather than passive.
A welcome of boiling water and burning in Hell-fire supplies a parallel arrival/reception frame, with contrary valence.
Those who return to forbidden conduct are told that Hell will suffice them; it links conduct, arrival, and evil return.
The Fire is guarded by stern angels who do not disobey, a strong secondary image of maintained, active custody.
Hell's punishment is assigned to those who disbelieve, and the verse calls it an evil destination.
Its roar and boiling when they are cast in give sensory force to entry into the prepared Fire.
Seizing and chaining the condemned makes the capture dimension explicit.
The command to burn him in Hell directly follows seizure and chain, forming a close capture-to-destination sequence.
The blaze is introduced as a refuge; the following portrayal makes it an active claimant of those who turn away.
The blaze calls for the one who turned and withdrew, a particularly close active-interception parallel.
The declaration of casting him into Saqar adds a direct threatened destination under a distinct Fire-name.
Saqar leaves nothing and spares nothing, adding the consuming severity of the punitive place.
Chains, iron collars, and a blaze are prepared for disbelievers, directly reinforcing prior punitive preparation.
Immediate continuation: the punishment is stated as a fitting requital, qualifying the watchpost as measured return.
Immediate continuation: denial of the signs supplies the stated conduct within the accountability sequence.
Immediate continuation: all things are enumerated in a record, directly supporting the individual accounting reading.
Immediate continuation: the command to taste and the increase of punishment portray the consequence as active and escalating.
Immediate contrary continuation: the reverent receive success, preserving the passage's differentiated outcomes.
The kindling of Hell is an immediate eschatological activation image for the prepared place.
The wicked are declared to be in Hell, directly identifying its assigned inhabitants.
Their entry on the recompense day ties Hell to the Day's enacted judgment.
Entry into the great Fire provides a direct destination parallel, though without the watchpost nuance.
Only the most wretched enters the blazing Fire, adding a sharply differentiated recipient class.
Calling the guards gives a secondary custodial image, but the scene is not an account of Hell itself.
